newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Workers collect the dead in eastern Zaire city.
newsitem.headline: Workers collect the dead in eastern Zaire city.

text.p: Red Cross workers on Tuesday collected some of hundreds of bodies of people killed in battles for the eastern Zairean city of Goma, now almost entirely under rebel control.
Andre Kissasse Ngandu, military head of the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, told a news conference the rebels controlled the city and its airport.

"We need you the international community to come here and help refugees and we are waiting...Access to the camps depends on the security situation but NGOs (non-governmental organisations) and humanitarian agencies are welcome," he said.
Zairean staff of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) said they could not reach camps for some 700,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees in the Goma region.

They said they had been stopped on the road to Mugunga camp by refugees who reported many dead there. Before the battle for Goma late last week, Mugunga was the largest refugee camp in the world with 400,000 residents.
Goma Central Hospital, which is on the western outskirts of the city, was still disputed between rival forces on Tuesday.
Rebel roadblocks were at all major exit routes from Goma.
Witnesses said three corpses lay at a checkpoint manned by members of the exiled Rwandan Hutu Interahamwe militia, which played a leading role in the 1994 genocide in Rwanda.
"There are over 400 of them (bodies) so far," said Kahindo Matos, a Zairean working for the IFRC at its looted office.
He said most of the dead found lying in the streets and buildings of eastern Zaire's largest border city were civilians but some of them were wearing items of military uniforms.
"We are collecting the bodies towards the airport for burial and are in the process of continuing the task of finding them. We expect many more by tonight," said Matos.
Rwandan troops thrust into Goma on Friday by land and boat across Lake Kivu backing rebel forces after Zairean troops bombarded the Rwandan border town of Gisenyi, diplomats said.
Reinforcements from the Rwanda Patriotic Army (RPA) escorted journalists into Goma on Saturday while those Zaireans not involved in the fighting took advantage of the chaos to loot.

The Rwandan government, however, has either flatly denied or played down the fact that troops of its Tutsi-dominated army were in Goma, the hub of relief efforts for more than a million refugees in eastern Zaire until aid workers fled on Saturday.
Rebels said fighting in Goma ended on Saturday when they seized the airport. Aid workers said a plane landed on Tuesday but they had no idea of its identity or who it was carrying.
Foreign journalists, allowed by rebels to cross into the city from Rwanda, heard shooting from light weapons in Goma but it was unclear who was responsible for the sporadic firing.
An IFRC list of 187 of the bodies from the fighting in Goma showed 162 were men, 16 were women and nine were children.
In the streets of the lakeside city, rebels drove around in U.N. aid agency vehicles, arresting or beating Zairean looters.
Children seized what they could from shops and some residents were out on the streets of what was a resort until it was flooded by Rwandan refugees in 1994.
The U.N. refugee agency headquarters building, a former bank, had been emptied by looters and was held by one very drunk rebel. The nearby Hotel du Lac was just starting to reopen.
